sections.Trust Boundaries: Boundary 1 (external client -> agent.py FastAPI app): HTTP POST /chat and /extract_tool_call accept a fully free-form `user_profile: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` from the caller with no schema validation, no authentication, and no signature/token check. Boundary 2 (agent.py -> LLM): `user_profile` is serialized as key/value bullet text into the system prompt via build_system_prompt() and sent to the LLM (ChatOpenAI, model/endpoint from env vars INFERENCE_MODEL/INFERENCE_BASE_URL/INFERENCE_API_KEY) — this is a prompt-text boundary, not a structured-data boundary; the LLM only 'respects' it as natural-language instruction. Boundary 3 (LLM -> MCP tool call): the LLM (or, in /extract_tool_call, llm_with_tools.ainvoke) decides which of the 3 registered tools to call and with what arguments; these become input.args.* structured values received by server.py's @mcp.tool() functions over stdio from agent.py's MultiServerMCPClient subprocess. Boundary 4 (server.py -> app.py business logic): server.py wrapper functions call getCarBrands/searchCarPrice/getCarsByType in app.py directly (in-process Python call, not a boundary requiring serialization). Boundary 5 (app.py -> external FIPE API): outbound HTTPS GET requests to https://parallelum.com.br/fipe/api/v1/... with no TLS pinning, no response signing/integrity check beyond HTTP 200 status check and JSON parse; response content is trusted verbatim and returned to the caller. No OPA or other pre-execution policy interception exists anywhere in the current code; user_role/user_name (declared in system_vars.json) are never read or referenced by any of the 4 source files — they exist only as conceptual policy-input placeholders, not as plumbed runtime data. The closest analog, user_profile, is unauthenticated client-supplied input that only reaches the LLM as prompt text, never as input.extensions.subject.* structured data nor as any tool argument.
sections.Data Flow: Request: HTTP client -> POST /chat {question, user_profile} (agent.py) -> build_system_prompt() interpolates user_profile into system prompt text -> agent.ainvoke() (LangGraph ReAct agent) -> LLM selects tool + generates input.args (brand_name / vehicle_type) -> MultiServerMCPClient invokes MCP tool over stdio -> server.py @mcp.tool() wrapper (input validation: strip/empty checks and default substitution only) -> app.py business function (getCarBrands/searchCarPrice/getCarsByType) -> outbound HTTPS GET to parallelum.com.br FIPE API (0-3+ chained calls per searchCarPrice invocation: brands lookup, model lookup, years lookup, price lookup). Response: FIPE JSON -> app.py formats into a markdown/emoji string -> returned through server.py tool return value -> LangGraph agent's tool-result message -> LLM composes final natural-language answer -> agent.py extracts result["messages"][-1].content -> ChatResponse JSON -> HTTP client. Alternate path (/extract_tool_call): same prompt construction, but llm_with_tools.ainvoke() returns the raw tool_calls[0] (name + args) directly as JSON without executing the tool or invoking app.py/FIPE at all — this endpoint is a policy/test-harness introspection path, not a production execution path.

Tool Arguments.Origin / influence: LLM-generated argument (via LangGraph tool-calling / llm_with_tools) based on the user's natural-language question; passed through server.py's search_car_price wrapper to app.py's searchCarPrice(query).
Tool Arguments.Disposition: Acts on — server.py strips whitespace and rejects empty/blank values with a canned message; app.py performs a case-insensitive substring match (`query_lower in brand['nome'].lower()`) against the live FIPE brand list to select a brand, then drives 3+ chained downstream FIPE calls. No canonicalization to Title Case is performed anywhere in code, contrary to what guidance assumes happens 'before the policy check.'

Tool Arguments.Origin / influence: LLM-generated argument, optional with schema default 'carros'; passed through server.py to app.py's getCarsByType(vehicle_type).
Tool Arguments.Disposition: Acts on, with a silent fallback: server.py defaults blank/whitespace-only input to 'carros' before calling app.py; app.py lower-cases the value and looks it up in a fixed type_mapping dict, silently defaulting ANY unrecognized value (including different casing such as 'Caminhoes') to 'carros' via `type_mapping.get(vehicle_type.lower(), 'carros')`. This confirms in code the guidance's explicit warning that the backend silently coerces unrecognized types and that policy must reject them rather than rely on that fallback.
